description: Error handling patterns are structured approaches to detect, propagate, and respond to errors in software systems. This skill covers techniques beyond basic exception handling, including return codes, errno patterns, and design patterns like Visitor for compile-time error checking. You'll learn how to design robust error handling that improves code reliability, maintainability, and debuggability, applicable across languages and paradigms.

core_concepts: Return Code and Errno Pattern: Using function return values and global error indicators to signal errors, common in C and systems programming.
Exception Handling: Structured mechanism using try-catch-finally blocks to separate error logic from normal flow, supported in many languages.
Visitor Pattern for Compile-Time Error Checking: Using the Visitor design pattern to enforce handling of all object types, generating compiler errors for unhandled cases.
Error Propagation Strategies: Techniques like error wrapping, chaining, and rethrowing to maintain context while passing errors up the call stack.
Result and Option Types: Using algebraic data types (e.g., Rust's Result, Haskell's Either) to represent success or failure without exceptions.
Error Recovery and Retry Patterns: Strategies for handling transient errors, such as exponential backoff and circuit breakers.

common_pitfalls.pitfall: Ignoring return codes or failing to check error indicators, leading to silent failures.
common_pitfalls.advice: Always check return values and errno after function calls that can fail; use static analysis tools to enforce checks.

common_pitfalls.pitfall: Overusing exceptions for control flow, making code hard to read and debug.
common_pitfalls.advice: Reserve exceptions for truly exceptional conditions; use return codes or result types for expected errors.

common_pitfalls.pitfall: Catching exceptions too broadly (e.g., catching Exception) and swallowing errors.
common_pitfalls.advice: Catch specific exception types and handle them appropriately; log or rethrow if you cannot recover.

common_pitfalls.pitfall: Not cleaning up resources in error paths, leading to leaks.
common_pitfalls.advice: Use RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) or finally blocks to ensure resources are released regardless of errors.

common_pitfalls.pitfall: Failing to update the Visitor pattern when new types are added, causing runtime errors.
common_pitfalls.advice: Use compile-time checks (e.g., abstract methods) to force implementation for all types; consider using pattern matching languages.
